tots.title: ¿Qué es la IA?
tots.summary: Objetivos: la IA es un amigo útil que aprende mirando imágenes.
contentBlocks: Historia: ¡Hola, pequeños! ¡Soy Sparki! La IA es como un perrito listo. Mira muchas fotos y aprende. ¡Mira cómo ordeno los bloques rojos! La IA nos ayuda, pero siempre preguntamos a un adulto primero.
Idea: La IA aprende mirando. Siempre preguntamos a un adulto.
Pausa: Ordena 5 bloques de colores. ¡Sparki aplaude cuando aciertas!
Regla: Guía para adultos: jueguen con bloques y digan: “¡La IA también nos ayuda a ordenar colores!”

activity.title: Ordena colores con Sparki
activity.description: Ordena 5 bloques de colores. ¡Aplaudan cada vez que acierten!

quizQuestions.prompt: La IA aprende de…
Sparki nos ayuda a…
Un patrón es…

thinkPrompts.label: ¡Piensa!
thinkPrompts.text: Señala el bloque rojo. Señala dos bloques que coincidan.

thinkPrompts.label: ¡Piensa!
thinkPrompts.text: Dile a un adulto: “¡La IA nos ayuda a ordenar!”

crew.title: ¿Qué es la IA?
crew.summary: Objetivos: la IA aprende con datos y puede equivocarse.
contentBlocks: Historia: La IA no es magia: estudia millones de ejemplos. Pero aún puede fallar. Por eso siempre verificamos con un adulto o con nuestro cerebro.
Idea: La IA aprende de datos. Los humanos tienen la última palabra.
Pausa: Debatir: “¿Puede la IA tener siempre razón?”
Regla: Guía para adultos: hablen de errores reales de la IA que hayan visto.

activity.title: Debate: ¿la IA puede acertar siempre?
activity.description: En parejas: argumenten a favor y en contra. Terminen con por qué los humanos revisan a la IA.

quizQuestions.prompt: La IA aprende principalmente de…
La historia de ordenar de Sparki se parece a…
¿Quién debe decidir en temas importantes?
options: Los humanos: nosotros y adultos de confianza

thinkPrompts.label: ¡Piensa en esto!
thinkPrompts.text: Nombra un error de IA que hayas oído. ¿Qué pasó?

thinkPrompts.label: ¡Piensa en esto!
thinkPrompts.text: ¿Por qué es buena la regla del “humano en el circuito”?

tots.title: Coding as Games
tots.summary: Learning goals: Coding is fun “if this, then that” rules.
contentBlocks: Story: Coding is silly games! If you clap, I jump. If I jump, you clap! Let’s use our bodies!
Idea: Coding is giving happy instructions.
Pause: Play “if you clap, then hop” with blocks or stuffed animals.
Rule: Parent guide: Play if-then games at snack time or bath time.

activity.title: If you clap, then hop
activity.description: Take turns being the “coder.” Say the rule and act it out together.

quizQuestions.prompt: Code is like…
options: A recipe or set of rules

quizQuestions.prompt: If the light is green, we…

thinkPrompts.label: Think!
thinkPrompts.text: Make one new if-then rule with your family.

crew.title: Coding as Games
crew.summary: Learning goals: Coding is logic and problem-solving.
contentBlocks: Story: Coding is powerful. One small change in code can fix a big problem or create one. Let’s build a simple game and see how logic works.
Idea: Code is powerful — think before you code.
Pause: Debug a broken “if-then” game: what happens when the condition is wrong?
Rule: Parent guide: Talk about how code affects real apps you use.

activity.title: Debug an if-then game
activity.description: Change one rule on purpose — predict what breaks. Fix it together.

quizQuestions.prompt: Code is like…
options: A recipe or set of rules

quizQuestions.prompt: What happens if the condition in your code is wrong?

thinkPrompts.label: Think about this!
thinkPrompts.text: Name one real app that depends on an if-then rule.

tots.title: Software Explorers
tots.summary: Learning goals: Software is the happy instructions inside apps.
contentBlocks: Story: Software is like the recipe for cookies! It tells the app how to show pictures and make sounds.
Idea: Every app has software inside.
Pause: Point to buttons on a simple app and say “Software helps this work!”
Rule: Parent guide: Point out software in your favorite apps together.

activity.title: Button hunt
activity.description: Open one kid-safe app. Tap three buttons and name what each makes happen.

quizQuestions.prompt: Which is software?
Software lives inside…

thinkPrompts.label: Think!
thinkPrompts.text: What sound or picture did software make happen today?

crew.title: Software Explorers
crew.summary: Learning goals: Software controls everything we use.
contentBlocks: Story: Software is the brain behind every app. Let’s explore how it makes decisions and why we need to understand it.
Idea: Software makes decisions for us — so we should know what it’s doing.
Pause: Map the software in 3 favorite apps: what inputs and outputs do you see?
Rule: Parent guide: Explore app settings together — what can you turn on or off?

activity.title: Software map
activity.description: Sketch 3 apps. For each, write what data goes in and what the app shows or does.

quizQuestions.prompt: Which is software?
Software “lives” in…

thinkPrompts.label: Think about this!
thinkPrompts.text: What is one decision an app made for you today?

tots.title: AI in Our World
tots.summary: Learning goals: AI helps people in nice ways.
contentBlocks: Story: AI helps doctors and farmers! It’s a helpful tool, but we always check with a grown-up.
Idea: AI is a helper. Grown-ups check it.
Pause: Match pictures (hospital, farm) to “AI helps here.”
Rule: Parent guide: Talk about helpful AI at home (like voice helpers).

activity.title: Picture match
activity.description: Use picture cards: point to places AI can help and name the grown-up who checks.

quizQuestions.prompt: AI can help people by…

thinkPrompts.label: Think!
thinkPrompts.text: Who checks if AI is right at our house?

crew.title: AI in Our World
crew.summary: Learning goals: AI helps but needs human oversight.
contentBlocks: Story: AI is in hospitals, farms, and schools. It’s powerful, but humans decide when it’s right or wrong.
Idea: AI is a tool — humans are the boss.
Pause: Research one real-world AI and list one pro and one con.
Rule: Parent guide: Discuss AI in a news story together.

activity.title: Real-world AI pros and cons
activity.description: Pick one AI tool you know. Write one benefit and one risk, then share with an adult.

quizQuestions.prompt: AI can help people by…

thinkPrompts.label: Think about this!
thinkPrompts.text: Who makes the final decision when AI is wrong?

tots.title: Kind & Fair Coding
tots.summary: Learning goals: We use code and AI with kindness.
contentBlocks: Story: We always choose kind! AI is only as kind as we make it.
Idea: Be kind with AI.
Pause: Choose kind picture cards vs mean ones.
Rule: Parent guide: Say kind words when using apps together.

activity.title: Kind or mean?
activity.description: Sort face or picture cards into “kind” and “mean.” Talk about how each feels.

quizQuestions.prompt: Who is responsible for how AI behaves?
options: The people who design and use it

thinkPrompts.label: Think!
thinkPrompts.text: Show a kind face to Sparki. What kind word can you say?

crew.title: Kind & Fair Coding
crew.summary: Learning goals: Code can be biased or unfair if humans aren’t careful.
contentBlocks: Story: Code is only as fair as the people who write it. We must choose kindness and fairness every time.
Idea: Humans control fairness.
Pause: Design one fair rule and one unfair rule for the same game.
Rule: Parent guide: Discuss bias in apps and social media at a kid-safe level.

activity.title: Fair vs unfair rules
activity.description: Write two game rules: one fair, one unfair. Explain who gets left out.

quizQuestions.prompt: Who is responsible for how AI behaves?
options: The people who design and use it

thinkPrompts.label: Think about this!
thinkPrompts.text: What is one way an app could be unfair to some kids?

tots.title: Privacy & Sharing Safely
tots.summary: Learning goals: Only share with family.
contentBlocks: Story: We keep our name and home private. Only show to family!
Idea: Private = for family only.
Pause: Sort pictures: “family okay” vs “stranger no.”
Rule: Parent guide: Practice “this stays in our house.”

activity.title: Family vs stranger sort
activity.description: Use drawings: smile for “share with family,” stop hand for “not for strangers.”

quizQuestions.prompt: Who should you ask before posting a picture online?
What should your account settings be?
options: Private to people you and a grown-up know

quizQuestions.prompt: Which information should you keep off your profile?
If a stranger sends you a message, what do you do?
options: Reply and make a new friend
Ignore, block, and tell a grown-up

quizQuestions.prompt: Who decides what you can post?
options: You and a trusted grown-up together

thinkPrompts.label: Think!
thinkPrompts.text: Name one thing we only share at home.

crew.title: Privacy & Sharing (Instagram-style)
crew.summary: Learning goals: Digital footprint lasts forever.
contentBlocks: Story: Everything you post creates a digital footprint. Think before you share — would you want this forever?
Idea: Privacy is your power.
Pause: “Forever or delete?” card sort — what should never be public?
Rule: Parent guide: Review privacy settings together.

activity.title: Forever or delete?
activity.description: List 5 post ideas. Mark each: OK forever, or never post.

quizQuestions.prompt: Who should you ask before posting a picture online?
What should your account settings be?
options: Private to people you and a grown-up know

tots.title: Kind Words Online
tots.summary: Learning goals: Kind words make everyone happy.
contentBlocks: Story: Mean words hurt. Kind words make friends!
Idea: Use kind words.
Pause: Say kind words to a Sparki plushie or stuffed friend.
Rule: Parent guide: Role-play kind comments together.

activity.title: Kind words to Sparki
activity.description: Take turns saying one kind sentence. Clap after each kind word.

quizQuestions.prompt: Before posting a video, you should…

thinkPrompts.label: Think!
thinkPrompts.text: Which word is kind: “great job” or “you’re dumb”?

crew.title: Kindness & Bystanders (short video apps)
crew.summary: Learning goals: Bystander intervention and upstanding.
contentBlocks: Story: Being kind online is an active choice. If you see bullying, you can block, report, or speak up kindly.
Idea: Kindness is a skill.
Pause: Role-play bystander scenarios with a partner.
Rule: Parent guide: Discuss real examples from social media at a kid-safe level.

activity.title: Bystander role-play
activity.description: Three scenarios: mean comment, pile-on, fake rumor. Practice block, report, and kind words.

quizQuestions.prompt: Before posting a video, you should…
Who should be able to see your videos?
options: Only people you and a grown-up know

quizQuestions.prompt: If someone leaves a mean comment, you can…
options: Block, report, and tell a grown-up

quizQuestions.prompt: What information should stay private?
When something online feels wrong, you should…
options: Tell a trusted grown-up right away

tots.title: Strangers in Games
tots.summary: Learning goals: Only talk to people we know.
contentBlocks: Story: If someone says hi and you don’t know them, tell a grown-up!
Idea: Strangers online = tell a grown-up.
Pause: Practice saying “I’ll ask my grown-up!”
Rule: Parent guide: Review “stranger = grown-up help.”

activity.title: I’ll ask my grown-up
activity.description: Practice the phrase loud and proud. High-five after each practice.

quizQuestions.prompt: What is okay to share in game chat?

quizQuestions.prompt: If a stranger invites you to a private game, you should…

quizQuestions.prompt: Games should make you feel…

crew.title: Strangers, Grooming & Red Flags (games)
crew.summary: Learning goals: Grooming signs and reporting.
contentBlocks: Story: Strangers online may pretend to be kids. Red flags: asking for photos, secrets, or meetings. Always tell a grown-up immediately.
Idea: Trust your gut and tell an adult.
Pause: Spot the red-flag conversation — what would you do?
Rule: Parent guide: Practice the “tell a trusted adult” script.

activity.title: Red-flag spotter
activity.description: Read short chat examples. Circle red flags and write who you tell.

tots.title: Screen Time & Healthy Habits
contentBlocks: Story: We play with screens a little, then run and play outside!
Idea: Balance screens and real play.
Pause: Timer game: screen time then jump time.
Rule: Parent guide: Set simple screen rules together.

activity.title: Timer then jump
activity.description: Short screen time, then 2 minutes of jumping or dancing. Repeat once.

quizQuestions.prompt: What is a safe kind of picture to send?

crew.title: Digital Wellness & Balance
crew.summary: Learning goals: Digital wellness and balance.
contentBlocks: Story: Screen time is fun, but our brains need movement, sleep, and real friends too. Let’s make a healthy screen plan.
Idea: Balance is key.
Pause: Create a personal screen-time schedule for school nights and weekends.
Rule: Parent guide: Co-create family media rules.

activity.title: My screen plan
activity.description: Block out homework, sleep, outside play, and screen time. Post it on the fridge.

tots.title: Loud Games & Grown-ups
tots.summary: Learning goals: Tell a grown-up if voices feel scary or mean.
contentBlocks: Story: In fast games, voices can get loud. If it feels yucky, pause and get a grown-up.
Idea: You never have to stay in a chat that feels bad.
Pause: Practice: “Grown-up, this voice feels mean.”
Rule: Parent guide: Sit together for the first voice-chat sessions.

activity.title: Grown-up helper phrase
activity.description: Say the helper phrase three times. Draw a picture of your grown-up next to you.

quizQuestions.prompt: Who is it safest to talk with in voice chat?
options: People you and a grown-up know

quizQuestions.prompt: If someone is yelling or being mean, you can…
options: Mute or leave and tell a grown-up

quizQuestions.prompt: Is it okay to tease if someone is upset?
options: No, we should be kind even in games

quizQuestions.prompt: Private info you should never share in voice chat includes…
Who can you talk to if a game makes you feel upset?

thinkPrompts.label: Think!
thinkPrompts.text: Show a thumbs up or thumbs down: did the voice chat feel safe?

crew.title: Voice Chat & Team Games
crew.summary: Learning goals: Boundaries, muting, and speaking up.
contentBlocks: Story: Fast games + voice chat need clear rules: who can talk, when to mute, and when to leave.
Idea: You control your mic and your peace.
Pause: Write your “mute and leave” plan before you queue up.
Rule: Parent guide: Co-create voice-chat rules for school nights.

activity.title: Voice chat plan
activity.description: List: mute triggers, break times, and who you tell if someone crosses a line.

thinkPrompts.label: Think about this!
thinkPrompts.text: When is muting braver than arguing?

tots.title: You Are a Safety Hero
tots.summary: Learning goals: You can keep yourself safe!
contentBlocks: Story: You are a Safety Hero! You know the rules and help others.
Idea: You are in charge of staying safe.
Pause: Make a “Hero Cape” with paper and cheer for one safe choice you made today.
Rule: Parent guide: Celebrate small safe choices daily.

activity.title: Hero cape cheer
activity.description: Decorate a paper cape. Name one safety rule you followed today.

crew.title: Leadership & Digital Safety Hero
contentBlocks: Story: You now know enough to protect yourself and help others. Being a Safety Hero means speaking up and teaching kindness.
Idea: You are powerful and responsible.
Pause: Design a “Safety Hero” poster or short video plan — what will you teach?
Rule: Parent guide: Celebrate and encourage leadership moments.

activity.title: Safety Hero poster or video
activity.description: Pick one rule (privacy, kindness, strangers, balance). Teach it to a friend or sibling.
